discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable neutral-atom arrays for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique / CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned the Rydberg blockade, a strong, controllable interaction between highly excited atoms, from a theoretical idea into a central platform of quantum science. Lukin developed the blockade concept for collective quantum control and later, with large reconfigurable tweezer arrays, demonstrated quantum simulation of exotic phases and logical qubits with error detection and correction. Browaeys and Saffman achieved the first observations of blockade between two individual atoms (2009) and pioneered deterministic atom-by-atom assembly of arrays, high-fidelity entangling gates and programmable quantum many-body simulators. Their work rests on clean, quantitatively testable light-matter physics: interactions predicted from first principles and confirmed with remarkable precision. Neutral-atom arrays now reach hundreds to thousands of qubits, linking AMO physics with condensed matter and quantum computing, and have changed how the community engineers and probes strongly interacting quantum matter.
